title: On the Scalability of Temporal Relative Positional Encoding for Dynamic Link Prediction

problem.claim: Dynamic link prediction methods need to model relationships between nodes using temporal graph structure and relative positional features.

gap.claim: Existing dynamic graph methods using TRPE have high computational costs and poor scalability, partly because neighborhood compression loses information.

contributions.claim: A scalable framework integrates TRPE computation with temporal clusters.
The framework replaces high-order relative position information with cluster-based computation and assigns nodes to clusters by structural role.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their framework makes TGNNs more expressive than existing dynamic graph learning methods and more scalable than existing TRPE models.
On seven standard temporal link prediction benchmarks, the authors report comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal graph neural networks with relative positional features improve relationship modeling for dynamic link prediction.
TRPE combines local subgraph computation with temporal decay effects.
Existing TRPE-based methods face computational and scalability limitations caused in part by neighborhood compression information loss.
The proposed framework uses temporal clusters, cluster-based computation, and structural-role-based node assignment to improve TRPE scalability.
The authors report improved expressiveness and scalability, with comparable or superior benchmark performance on seven temporal link prediction datasets.

source_observation.claim: Cluster-based computation and structural-role-based assignment are used to reduce computation costs and information loss during neighborhood compression.

interpretation.claim: Structured compression may preserve more useful graph information than random neighborhood sketches while improving scalability.

application.claim: For scalable dynamic graph learning, consider grouping nodes by structural role before compressing high-order positional information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when structural-role-based clustering fails or how its costs compare across graph types.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the temporal clustering algorithm.
The abstract does not report dataset names, quantitative results, or computational measurements.
The abstract does not describe ablations, implementation details, or limitations.
